messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Respond with exactly {"code": "<letter><digit><digit>", "condition": "<short name>"} and no other text.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:
Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital stay: The patient was admitted to the hospital due to the presence of a brain tumor located in the clivus region. He underwent surgical intervention via a left suboccipital craniotomy, which involved resection of the tumor. Oral intubation was done using the Macintosh laryngoscope blade, and the patient was placed in the left park bench position with neck flexion. Surgery was performed via the left lateral suboccipital approach. The lesion was decompressed, and the operation was completed successfully.

Medical Condition at Discharge: The patient had minor swelling in the neck, tongue, and pharynx on the left side. He experienced pain in the tip of his tongue with a small ulcer on the left side after returning to the intensive care unit. The swelling of his tongue gradually improved after the administration of steroids. The patient was discharged 10 days after the surgery.

Follow-Up Care: The patient was advised to undergo follow-up MRI after three months of surgery as well as clinical follow-up as per physician's recommendations.

Discharge Medications: None.

Instructions: The patient was advised to follow-up with his physician for regular check-up and take rest until complete recovery.
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]

Respond with the JSON object only, starting with { and ending with }.

text:
The tumor is in the clivus, which is skull base bone, but the histology is not stated. Clival tumors are most often chordoma (C41.0, malignant neoplasm of bones of skull and face) or chondrosarcoma, and the summary calls it a "brain tumor" without specifying type. Because the diagnosis section is withheld, I have to pick the most likely category. A clival tumor of unspecified nature falls under D49 (neoplasm of unspecified behavior), but the course makes a specific diagnosis more likely. Chordoma is the classic clival tumor, so C41 is plausible. Meningioma is also possible, since petroclival and clival meningiomas are common and the approach used (lateral suboccipital) suits them, which would give D32. The left park bench position and the lateral suboccipital approach point toward a petroclival lesion, and meningioma is the most common tumor there. I'll choose meningioma (D32, benign neoplasm of meninges).

{"code": "D32", "condition": "Benign neoplasm of cerebral meninges (clival meningioma)"}
